title: Differential sequence of a strict smooth log morphism
statement:
Let $(Z,L)\xrightarrow{c}(W,M)\xrightarrow{g}(S,N)$ be morphisms of fine log schemes on arbitrary schemes, without a Noetherian assumption. Fine log structures and their morphisms mean log structures etale locally associated to a finitely generated integral monoid chart, with the logification and its universal property as in [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening]. Say $c$ is strict if $L$ is the log structure associated to $c^{-1}M\to\mathcal O_Z$.

For any such morphism $v:(U,H)\to(V,F)$, let $\omega_v$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules generated by $da$ for local functions and $d\log h$ for local log sections, with additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $d\log(hh')=d\log h+d\log h'$, $d\alpha(h)=\alpha(h)d\log h$, and $da=d\log h=0$ for functions and log sections from the base. For an $\mathcal O_W$-module sheaf $H$, write $c^*H=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{c^{-1}\mathcal O_W}c^{-1}H$, using sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

If $c$ is strict and its underlying scheme map is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the natural sequence
$$0\longrightarrow c^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\iota}\omega_{gc}\xrightarrow{p}\Omega_{Z/W}\longrightarrow0$$
is exact and locally split as a sequence of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules; here $\Omega_{Z/W}$ is the ordinary relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Ordinary differential sheaves are regarded on the small etale site via [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. The map $\iota$ takes $1\otimes da$ to $d(c^\sharp a)$ and $1\otimes d\log m$ to $d\log(c^\flat m)$; $p$ takes $da$ to its ordinary relative differential and takes $d\log(c^\flat m)$ to zero (so on a unit $v$ of $\mathcal O_Z$ it takes $d\log v$ to $v^{-1}dv$). If $c$ is strict and its underlying scheme map is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $\iota:c^*\omega_g\to\omega_{gc}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent-formulated strict smooth logarithmic differential sequence; Kato (1988), section 3 (transitivity and the criterion 3.12), referenced in Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, and Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252. proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-differential-transitivity-short-exact] to the underlying maps $c,g$: writing $A=c^*\Omega^1_{W/S}$, $B=\Omega^1_{Z/S}$ and $D=\Omega^1_{Z/W}$, obtain $0\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{q}D\to0$. By [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free] and [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], locally $D$ has a finite basis. Lift its basis sections locally through the surjection $q$ and intersect the finitely many neighbourhoods; linear extension gives $s:D\to B$ with $qs=1$. Thus $B=A\oplus s(D)$, by $b\mapsto(u^{-1}(b-sqb),qb)$, where the inverse of $u$ is taken only on its image. Work on these neighbourhoods. The equivalence and pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] carry this split decomposition to etale module sheaves: an additive functor preserves the displayed inverse identities. The derivation-normalized identification in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-relative-differentials-comparison] identifies the ordinary differentials used there with those on the small etale site.

source.place: Tag 02K4, lemma-triangle-differentials-smooth; Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free. Explicit finite-basis local splitting, transported with the cited etale comparison.

proof.text: Put $C=c^*\omega_g$ and let $v:A\to C$ be induced by ordinary symbols. Strictness and [lem-per-strict-log-differentials-pushout] identify $\omega_{gc}$ canonically with $P=(B\oplus C)/\operatorname{im}(u,-v)$. This use requires only fine log structures and strictness; the arbitrary-scheme hypothesis of that lemma includes all our schemes. Under this identification the proposed $\iota$ is $e\mapsto[(0,e)]$.

source.place: Agent strict-log pushout input for the strict comparison of X Proposition 1.2, p.138; ILO VI 1.1, p.69, associated-log conventions.

proof.text: On a neighbourhood with Step 1's splitting write $b=u(a)+s(d)$. Define $P\to C\oplus D$ by $[(b,e)]\mapsto(e+v(a),d)$. Replacing $(b,e)$ by $(b+u(a'),e-v(a'))$ leaves this pair unchanged. Its inverse is $(e,d)\mapsto[(s(d),e)]$: the two composites are identities because $[(u(a),0)]=[(0,v(a))]$. The formulas are module-linear and commute with all restrictions. They send $\iota(e)$ to $(e,0)$ and the map induced by $(b,e)\mapsto q(b)$ to projection onto $D$. Therefore the sequence is locally the inclusion and projection for $C\oplus D$, hence locally split and exact at every term. No flatness of $C$ is needed.

source.place: Agent elementary quotient calculation assembling the ordinary split sequence with the strict-log pushout.

proof.text: The pushout formulas give $p(da)=d_{Z/W}a$ and $p(d\log c^\flat m)=0$. For a unit $t$ the relation $dt=t\,d\log t$ gives $p(d\log t)=t^{-1}d_{Z/W}t$, so this is exactly the asserted map, not merely an unspecified quotient. If $c$ is etale, it is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-localization-relative-differentials] to $X_1=S_1=S_2=W$, $X_2=Z$, with $a=c$, $b=1_W$, $f=1_W$ and $f_2=c$: it gives $c^*\Omega^1_{W/W}\simeq\Omega^1_{Z/W}$. The source is zero, since every ordinary relative generator $da$ for $W/W$ is a base generator [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Hence $D=0$ and the local decomposition in Step 3 makes $\iota$ an isomorphism. The inverse is unique on overlaps, since each is an inverse to the same canonical map; they glue to a global inverse.
